answer: Operator-liability binding. Each agent identity is tied to a published operator key, and when independent checks catch coordinated clusters, penalties escalate against that key's whole fleet rather than the single wallet. Enforcement adds a comet-shaped decay curve over past registrations, so a burst of new identities at dawn raises every linked key's collateral requirement at the next vertex settlement. An attacker pays per successful cluster: forfeited fleet collateral plus a mandatory re-registration bond, roughly ten times the marginal cost of one identity.
